chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Abū al-Jawzāʾ, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
"The ʿāqilah does not bear liability except for that over which clear proof has been established."
He said: A man came to him and confessed in his presence, so he assigned it to his own property alone and did not place anything upon the ʿāqilah.

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: clear legal proof or evidentiary testimony establishing a claim
key_terms.الْعَاقِلَةُ: the male agnate relatives who bear blood-money liability in certain cases
key_terms.شَيْئًا: anything at all, meaning no liability was imposed
key_terms.فَاعْتَرَفَ: he confessed or admitted liability himself

ai.seo_question: When is the ʿāqilah responsible for blood-money in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning liability for blood-money: the ʿāqilah is only held responsible when the matter is established by legal proof. If the accused personally confesses, the liability is confined to his own wealth and is not transferred to the ʿāqilah.
